newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: PM RUSHED BY PROTESTERS
In Sydney, a group of protesters has rushed the Prime Minister and his security officers as he entered a University hall to deliver a graduation lecture.
Police have called for backup at the Sydney University.
About 40 students sat down on the road leading to the Great Hall as the official car arrived, and police tried to drag them away.
But when John Howard left the car to go in a side entrance, the students rushed him.
They are protesting rises to higher education fees, and are calling on Mr Howard to leave the campus.
BLACKHAWK INQUIRY CONTINUES TODAY
A military Board of Inquiry into the Blackhawk helicopter disaster continues in Townsville today.
The inquiry yesterday heard that two Blackhawks changed direction and turned into each other with the main manoeuver being carried by the flight lead, Blackhawk one.
The pilot who witnessed the mid-air collision, Captain Matthew Barker, gave an emotional account of the crash.
Captain Barker was flying directly behind Blackhawk two, and he said he saw it turn left and Blackhawk one move right.
He said he screamed they were going to collide, and less than half a second later they did.
He said he saw a fireball and had to increase power and pull up to avoid the airbourne debris.
Under questioning he said the main move was done by Blackhawk one but he had no idea what caused them to make a major change in direction.
ABC BANNED FROM HANSON ADDRESS
The ABC has been banned from a function where federal Independent MP Pauline Hanson is speaking, which all other media are free to attend.
The National Party organisers say they agreed to Ms Hanson's demand that the ABC be excluded from the morning tea organised by the women's section of the Bribie Island branch.
A group of Aboriginal protesters has gathered outside the venue.
One hundred and eighty people are expected at the function, and another thirty to forty were turned away.
SUNSET BOULEVARD MUSICAL DIRECTOR DIES
The musical "Sunset Boulevard" will open at Melbourne's Regent theatre tomorrow despite the death of its musical director in a hit-run accident in Carlton last night.
The man died after his motorbike collided with a car on the corner of Rathdowne and Elgin Streets at one o'clock and veered into a power pole.
Police are looking for the driver of a white sedan which did not stop.
The death has rocked the arts community and Melbourne Festival Director, Leo Scofield, says it's a major blow to the Sunset cast.
The official opening of "Sunset Boulevard" has already been delayed by an illness of its star, Debra Byrne.
The actor, who had an ear infection, fell on stage during Monday's preview, forcing the show, as well as a charity performance, to be cancelled.
She has since been declared as in good health.
"RECLAIM THE NIGHT" MARCH IN BRISBANE
The organiser of tonight's 20th anniversary "Reclaim the Night" march in Brisbane says the event is more relevant today than it was 20 years ago.
Caroline Ride says that's because society is currently experiencing a backlash against women's rights, against feminism, and against talking about sexual violence.
Hundreds of women and children are expected to march through the city to Southbank to raise awareness about sexual violence.
ATTORNEYS-GENERAL MEET TO DISCUSS JOINT SCHEME
The State and Territory Attorneys-General say they're ready to take a united front against Federal Government plans to cut 25 per cent of their legal aid funding scheme with the Commonwealth.
Federal Attorney General, Daryl Williams, says the States should contribute more.
New South Wales Attorney-General, Jeff Shaw, plans to withdraw from the scheme, and the ACT is also considering such a move.
But Victorian Attorney-General Jan Wade, says she doesn't support the plan.
Mrs Wade doesn't want to end the current arrangments, believing they're the most efficient way to provide legal aid.
CROCODILE WATCH ON WORKERS
In North Queensland, earthmoving contractors working on the Banks of the Barron River near Cairns are under surveillance by a four meter crocodile.
The workers say the giant croc moves up and down the river eyeing them off.
They say they've been shaken by the crocodile's interest and want it removed from the area.
